insights: The table has 10,299 rows and 563 columns: one target column, one subject identifier, and 561 engineered motion-sensor features.
The target 'activity' has 6 unique labels, matching the described activity-recognition objective.
The 'subject' column has 30 unique IDs and should be treated as a person identifier for grouping, not as a predictive sensor feature.
No timestamp column is present, so a temporal split is not applicable; a group split by subject is the appropriate way to evaluate performance on unseen people.
The detailed profile covers only a prefix of columns, but the full schema contains all 561 sensor features; the plan should not truncate to the profiled prefix.
Sitting and standing are likely to be the most confusable classes in this sensor setting, so class-specific confusion diagnostics are important alongside macro F1.
Class counts are not provided in the profile, so imbalance should be checked before considering resampling or class-weight changes.
The features are high-dimensional and likely correlated; tree ensembles are a strong initial choice, while a regularized linear model provides a low-capacity control after standard scaling.
questions: Should sitting versus standing be monitored only through the 6-class confusion matrix, or would you also like a secondary derived binary diagnostic for that pair?
If class imbalance is found, should the first trial remain unweighted, or should class weighting be considered early to reduce sitting/standing confusion?
next_config.preparation: No joins or derived columns are needed. Use the single uploaded table. Retain all 561 numeric sensor features and exclude the target column 'activity' and the group column 'subject'. Use a reproducible group holdout by 'subject' so the same person does not appear in both training and validation/final evaluation. Apply standard preprocessing initially: median imputation, bounded one-hot encoding, and scaling. No augmentations are proposed for the first trial.
next_config.rationale: The objective is to predict activity for unseen people, so the validation design must keep subjects disjoint. A group holdout by 'subject' directly tests generalization to new persons and avoids leakage from repeated measurements of the same individual. Macro F1 is the appropriate primary metric because it treats all six activity classes equally and is sensitive to confusion between less frequent or visually similar activities such as sitting and standing. All 561 provided sensor features are retained because they are already engineered and the user explicitly asked not to truncate to the profiled prefix. Random Forest, LightGBM, and XGBoost are strong CPU tabular baselines for high-dimensional correlated features, while the regularized linear classifier provides a simple scaled control. Standard preprocessing is used initially as requested; later trials can use confusion-matrix diagnostics, feature subsets, or model-specific parameters if sitting/standing confusion remains high.
